note: Step 2 (model judgment + verified research): one place per candidate, decided by Claude Code (Fable 5.1) in the building session on 2026-11-03 after opening the pages listed in place_sources. 'opened' says what was actually read. Rule: for an imagined work, the place of composition if a source documents it; else first publication or first performance; for a legend, where the tradition locates it, certainty low. For a machine, where it was built, exhibited, or (for software) the organisation's headquarters. 'speaks' is whether the made being in the work speaks or converses: yes | no | unclear | n/a. Coordinates come from step 3, never from this file.
researcher: Claude Code, Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), in-session; no API calls

iliad-golden-handmaidens.place_label: Ionia: Smyrna (İzmir) or Chios, by tradition
iliad-golden-handmaidens.place_note: No place of composition is known. Ancient tradition made Homer a blind bard from Ionia; Pindar named Chios and Smyrna. Drawn at Smyrna as a placement for the Ionian tradition, not a fact.
iliad-golden-handmaidens.opened: Wikipedia 'Homer': 'the most widespread that he was a blind bard from Ionia'; Pindar: 'Homer originated from Chios and Smyrna'; all accounts 'historically apocryphal'.
iliad-golden-handmaidens.speaks_note: Iliad 18: the golden attendants have intelligence, voice, and strength (per the use-case 03 description).

argonautica-talos.place_label: Alexandria (Apollonius's library post); the myth sets Talos on Crete
argonautica-talos.place_note: Apollonius was a pupil of Callimachus and held a post at the Library of Alexandria; the Lives say he redrafted the poem at Rhodes. The bronze guardian himself belongs to Crete.
argonautica-talos.opened: Wikipedia 'Apollonius of Rhodes' (Alexandria librarian; 'redrafted the Argonautica ... at Rhodes'); 'Talos' ('protected Crete from pirates and invaders').
argonautica-talos.speaks_note: In Apollonius Talos hurls boulders at the Argo; no speech is recorded.

ovid-pygmalion.place_note: Ovid had completed the Metamorphoses by 8 CE, the year he was banished from Rome to Tomis. Wikipedia does not say where he wrote it; Rome is inferred from his residence until exile.
ovid-pygmalion.opened: Wikipedia 'Ovid': 'By AD 8, Ovid had completed Metamorphoses'; 'In AD 8, Ovid was banished to Tomis'.
ovid-pygmalion.speaks_note: The ivory statue comes to life; Ovid gives her no words.

liezi-yan-shi.place_label: Jiankang (Nanjing), capital of the Eastern Jin, under which the received text was compiled
liezi-yan-shi.place_note: All received Liezi texts derive from Zhang Zhan's edition (c. 370 CE), made under the Eastern Jin, whose capital was Jiankang. Zhang's own whereabouts are not recorded; the tale itself is set centuries earlier at the court of King Mu of Zhou.
liezi-yan-shi.opened: Wikipedia 'Liezi': 'All received Liezi texts derive from Zhang's version'; 'Eastern Jin': capital 'Jiankang (modern Nanjing)', 317–420.
liezi-yan-shi.speaks_note: In the tale the artificial man sings in tune and dances; whether it speaks is not stated in the sources opened.

talmud-rava-golem.place_label: Mahoza, a suburb of Ctesiphon (near Baghdad)
talmud-rava-golem.place_note: Sanhedrin 65b: Rava, who founded a school at Mahoza, creates a man and sends him to Rav Zeira. Drawn at Ctesiphon (Al-Mada'in, 35 km southeast of Baghdad) as the region of the Babylonian academies, not a documented spot; the Talmud's redaction (c. 500–550) has no single place.
talmud-rava-golem.opened: Wikipedia 'Rava (amora)': 'born about 280 CE in Mahoza (a suburb of Ctesiphon ...)'; 'Rava founded a school of his own in Mahoza'. 'Ctesiphon': '35 km (22 mi) southeast of the modern city of Baghdad'.
talmud-rava-golem.speaks_note: Rav Zeira speaks to the created man; it does not answer, and he returns it to dust.

al-jazari-automata.place_note: Chief engineer at the Artuqid court in Amid, modern Diyarbakır, where he finished the book on 16 January 1206 at Nasir al-Din Mahmud's request. Wikipedia's lead names the Artuklu Palace of the 'Mardin branch' of the Artuqids; Muslim Heritage and the Public Domain Review place him at Amid.
al-jazari-automata.opened: Wikipedia 'Ismail al-Jazari' (chief engineer at the Artuklu Palace; book 1206); web search summary of Muslim Heritage and Public Domain Review ('employed at the Artuqid court in the city of Diyarbakır (then called Amid)').
al-jazari-automata.speaks_note: Drink-serving and musical automata; birds that sing. No speaking device.

albertus-talking-head.place_label: Cologne (legend; the sources name no place)
albertus-talking-head.place_note: The brazen-head legend attaches to Albertus Magnus but names no city; Cologne, where he taught and died in 1280, is used as a placement. Wikipedia's article on Albertus does not mention the legend at all.
albertus-talking-head.opened: Wikipedia 'Brazen head': 'a head with a human voice and breath ... Thomas Aquinas destroyed it for continually interrupting'; 'Albertus Magnus': 'died on 15 November 1280 in the Dominican convent in Cologne'.
albertus-talking-head.speaks_note: The whole point of the legend: a head 'with a human voice' that talked too much.

vaucanson-flute-player.place_note: Presented to the Académie des Sciences in early 1738.
vaucanson-flute-player.opened: Wikipedia 'Jacques de Vaucanson': 'in early 1738, he presented his creation to the Académie des Sciences'.
vaucanson-flute-player.speaks_note: It plays the flute; none of Vaucanson's automata spoke.

mechanical-turk.place_note: Debut in 1770 at Schönbrunn Palace; Kempelen's home was Pressburg (Bratislava). A voice box saying 'Échec!' was added only after Mälzel bought it in 1805.
mechanical-turk.opened: Wikipedia 'Mechanical Turk': 'The Turk made its debut in 1770 at Schönbrunn Palace'; 'A voice box was added following the Turk's acquisition by Mälzel'.
mechanical-turk.speaks_note: Silent at its debut; one word ('Échec!') after 1805, and a human inside throughout.

jaquet-droz-writer.place_note: The three automata were presented at La Chaux-de-Fonds in 1774 according to the Jaquet Droz company history; the Wikipedia article says only that they are now in the Musée d'Art et d'Histoire, Neuchâtel.
jaquet-droz-writer.opened: Wikipedia 'Jaquet-Droz automata' (built 1768–1774; kept in Neuchâtel); web search summary of jaquet-droz.com ('presented in La Chaux-de-Fonds in 1774').
jaquet-droz-writer.speaks_note: It writes up to forty characters; it does not speak.

hoffmann-sandman.place_note: Hoffmann returned to Berlin in September 1814 and was living there when Nachtstücke appeared (1816–17) from Reimer. The story article names the publisher but no city.
hoffmann-sandman.opened: Wikipedia 'The Sandman (short story)' (Night Pieces, Reimer, 1816); 'E. T. A. Hoffmann': 'At the end of September 1814 ... Hoffmann returned to Berlin'.
hoffmann-sandman.speaks_note: Olimpia says only 'Ah, ah!'; Nathanael hears understanding in it.

poe-maelzel.place_note: April 1836 issue of the Southern Literary Messenger, published in Richmond; Poe was its editor from December 1835 to January 1837.
poe-maelzel.opened: Wikipedia 'Maelzel's Chess Player' ('originally published in the April 1836 issue'); 'Southern Literary Messenger' ('published in Richmond, Virginia'; 'By December, Poe was made editor').
poe-maelzel.speaks_note: An essay exposing a chess automaton; the machine does not speak.

hawthorne-artist-beautiful.place_note: Hawthorne lived at the Old Manse 1842–45 and wrote most of the tales of Mosses from an Old Manse there; this one first appeared in the Democratic Review, June 1844.
hawthorne-artist-beautiful.opened: Wikipedia 'The Artist of the Beautiful' (Democratic Review, June 1844); 'Nathaniel Hawthorne': 'At the Old Manse, Hawthorne wrote most of the tales collected in Mosses from an Old Manse'.
hawthorne-artist-beautiful.speaks_note: A mechanical butterfly; it moves, it does not speak.

butler-erewhon.geocode_query: Paternoster Square, City of London, London
butler-erewhon.place_note: Title page of the 1872 first edition: 'London: Trübner & Co., 60 Paternoster Row'. The machine chapters grew from letters to The Press, Christchurch, New Zealand.
butler-erewhon.opened: Wikipedia 'Erewhon' (Trübner and Ballantyne; articles in The Press, Christchurch); web search summary of the Wikisource/Internet Archive title page ('LONDON TRÜBNER & CO., 60 PATERNOSTER ROW 1872').
butler-erewhon.speaks_note: 'The Book of the Machines' argues that machines may develop consciousness; none speaks.

villiers-eve-future.place_note: Villiers lived in Paris from 1860; Léon Bloy says he wrote L'Ève future lying on bare floorboards after the bailiffs took his furniture. Wikipedia gives no publisher or city for the 1886 book.
villiers-eve-future.opened: Wikipedia 'The Future Eve'; 'Auguste Villiers de l'Isle-Adam' ('living in Paris since 1860'; the Bloy anecdote).
villiers-eve-future.speaks_note: Edison's android Hadaly talks; the novel is largely her conversation.

bierce-moxons-master.opened: Wikipedia 'Moxon's Master': 'first published in The San Francisco Examiner on April 16, 1899'.
bierce-moxons-master.speaks_note: The chess automaton strangles its maker; it does not speak.

baum-tik-tok.place_note: Reilly & Britton, Baum's Chicago publisher under an exclusive contract from 1904, issued Ozma of Oz in 1907.
baum-tik-tok.opened: Wikipedia 'Ozma of Oz' (Reilly & Britton, 1907); 'Reilly & Lee' (headquarters Chicago; the Oz contract).
baum-tik-tok.speaks_note: Tik-Tok talks when wound; he tells Dorothy where she is.

forster-machine-stops.place_label: London (The Oxford and Cambridge Review, Archibald Constable)
forster-machine-stops.place_note: The Oxford and Cambridge Review was published in London by Archibald Constable & Co., 1907–12 (HathiTrust catalogue record); the story appeared in its November 1909 number.
forster-machine-stops.opened: Wikipedia 'The Machine Stops' (Oxford and Cambridge Review, November 1909); web search summary of the HathiTrust record ('published in London by Archibald Constable & Co.').
forster-machine-stops.speaks_note: People speak to the Machine and consult its Book; whether the Machine answers in words is not settled by the sources opened.

metropolis-film.place_note: Premiered at the Ufa-Palast am Zoo, Berlin, 10 January 1927 (verified in the timeline (maps/02-ai-and-literature-timeline) against the Berlinale programme).
metropolis-film.opened: The timeline (maps/02-ai-and-literature-timeline)'s check note (Berlinale 2010 programme; Wikipedia 'Ufa-Palast am Zoo').
metropolis-film.speaks_note: The false Maria speaks, in a silent film's intertitles.

asimov-runaround.place_label: New York, Street & Smith (Astounding Science Fiction)
asimov-runaround.place_note: Astounding, March 1942, published by Street & Smith from 79 Seventh Avenue, Manhattan.
asimov-runaround.opened: Wikipedia 'Astounding Science Fiction' (Street & Smith); 'Street & Smith' ('headquarters was at 79 Seventh Avenue in Manhattan').
asimov-runaround.speaks_note: Speedy the robot talks, and recites Gilbert and Sullivan when confused.

asimov-i-robot.place_note: Gnome Press, Inc., 80 E. 11th St., New York, 1950.
asimov-i-robot.opened: Wikipedia 'Gnome Press': 'The address was Gnome Press, Inc., 80 E. 11th St. New York 3, N.Y.'; 'the first to publish Isaac Asimov's I, Robot'.
asimov-i-robot.speaks_note: The robots talk; the stories are their conversations with Susan Calvin.

forbidden-planet.place_label: Charlotte, North Carolina (premiere); filmed at MGM, Culver City
forbidden-planet.place_note: Premiered at a science fiction convention in Charlotte, 3–4 March 1956, before opening in more than 100 cities on 23 March; the sets were built on MGM's Culver City lot.
forbidden-planet.opened: Wikipedia 'Forbidden Planet': premiere 'in Charlotte, North Carolina on March 3-4, 1956'; 'sets ... constructed on a Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer (MGM) sound stage at its Culver City film lot'.
forbidden-planet.speaks_note: Robby the Robot, voiced by Marvin Miller.

lem-cyberiad.opened: Wikipedia 'The Cyberiad' ('1965 Polish collection Cyberiada by Wydawnictwo Literackie'); 'Wydawnictwo Literackie' ('a Kraków-based Polish publishing house').
lem-cyberiad.speaks_note: Trurl and Klapaucius are robots who talk throughout; one story builds a machine that writes poetry.

dick-androids.place_note: Doubleday, 1968; the firm was headquartered in Garden City, Long Island, from 1910 to 1986.
dick-androids.opened: Wikipedia 'Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?' (Publisher: Doubleday); 'Doubleday (publisher)' ('moved its operations ... to Garden City, New York' in 1910; headquartered there 'until 1986').
dick-androids.speaks_note: The androids pass for human in conversation; the Voigt-Kampff test is an interview.

kubrick-2001.place_note: Premiered at the Uptown Theater, Washington, D.C., 2 April 1968 (verified in the timeline (maps/02-ai-and-literature-timeline)).
kubrick-2001.opened: The timeline (maps/02-ai-and-literature-timeline)'s check note ('Premiered at the Uptown Theater, 2 April 1968').

blade-runner.place_label: Burbank, Warner Bros. Studios (sets); downtown Los Angeles locations
blade-runner.place_note: Released in 1,290 theaters across North America on 25 June 1982 with no single premiere recorded in the article; the 2019 street sets stood on the Warner Bros. lot in Burbank, with locations at the Bradbury Building and 2nd Street Tunnel.
blade-runner.opened: Wikipedia 'Blade Runner': 'a Warner Bros. backlot housed the 2019 Los Angeles street sets'; 'released in 1,290 theaters on June 25, 1982'.

gibson-neuromancer.place_note: Ace Books, New York, 1984; Wikipedia does not say where Gibson wrote it.
gibson-neuromancer.opened: Wikipedia 'Neuromancer' (infobox: Ace Books); 'Ace Books' ('founded in New York City in 1952'; headquarters New York City).
gibson-neuromancer.speaks_note: Wintermute speaks to Case through phones, screens, and borrowed faces.

piercy-he-she-it.opened: Wikipedia 'He, She and It' (Knopf, 1991); 'Alfred A. Knopf' (headquarters 'New York City, U.S.').
piercy-he-she-it.speaks_note: Yod the cyborg converses; the novel pairs him with the Prague golem Joseph, who learns to read and write.

powers-galatea.place_label: New York (Harper Perennial, per Wikipedia's infobox)
powers-galatea.place_note: Wikipedia's infobox gives Harper Perennial (New York) as publisher; the novel is set at a thinly veiled University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign.
powers-galatea.opened: Wikipedia 'Galatea 2.2' (Publisher: Harper Perennial; set at 'U.'); 'Harper Perennial' (headquarters 'New York City, New York').
powers-galatea.speaks_note: Helen, the neural network, is taught to read literature and converses with the narrator.

spielberg-ai.place_note: Premiered at the Venice Film Festival in 2001; US release 29 June 2001; produced by Warner Bros., DreamWorks, Amblin, and Stanley Kubrick Productions.
spielberg-ai.opened: Wikipedia 'A.I. Artificial Intelligence': 'premiered at the Venice Film Festival in 2001'.
spielberg-ai.speaks_note: David, the android boy, pleads for his life and asks the Blue Fairy to make him real.

chiang-lifecycle.place_note: Subterranean Press, a small press in Burton, Michigan, 2010.
chiang-lifecycle.opened: Wikipedia 'The Lifecycle of Software Objects' (Subterranean Press, 2010); 'Subterranean Press' ('a small press publisher in Burton, Michigan').
chiang-lifecycle.speaks_note: The digients 'have rudimentary speech' and learn more over the years.

jonze-her.place_label: New York, Lincoln Center (New York Film Festival)
jonze-her.place_note: World premiere as the closing-night film of the New York Film Festival, 12 October 2013 (verified in the timeline (maps/02-ai-and-literature-timeline) against the Film Society of Lincoln Center).
jonze-her.opened: The timeline (maps/02-ai-and-literature-timeline)'s check note (Film Society of Lincoln Center; Hollywood Reporter).
jonze-her.speaks_note: Samantha is a voice; the film is a conversation.

garland-ex-machina.place_note: Premiere at BFI Southbank on 16 December 2014; UK release 21 January 2015 (verified in the timeline (maps/02-ai-and-literature-timeline)).
garland-ex-machina.opened: The timeline (maps/02-ai-and-literature-timeline)'s check note ('after a BFI Southbank premiere on 16 December 2014').
garland-ex-machina.speaks_note: Ava; the film is a week of Turing-test conversations.

mcewan-machines-like-me.opened: Wikipedia 'Machines Like Me' (Jonathan Cape, 2019); 'Jonathan Cape' (headquarters 'London, England').
mcewan-machines-like-me.speaks_note: Adam, the synthetic human, talks, argues, and writes haiku.

ishiguro-klara.place_note: Faber and Faber (London) and Knopf (New York), 2 March 2021; drawn at the UK publisher.
ishiguro-klara.opened: Wikipedia 'Klara and the Sun' ('published on 2 March 2021 by Faber and Faber (UK) and Alfred A. Knopf (US)'); 'Faber and Faber' (headquarters London).

plato-phaedrus.place_label: Athens: the Academy; the dialogue is set by the Ilissos outside the walls
plato-phaedrus.place_note: Plato wrote most of the dialogues at the Academy in Athens between 383 and 366 BCE; the conversation itself takes place by a stream under a plane tree outside the city.
plato-phaedrus.opened: Wikipedia 'Plato': 'From 383 BC until about 366 BC, Plato primarily spent his time at the Academy, writing the majority of the dialogues'; 'Phaedrus (dialogue)': 'They sit by a stream under a plane tree and a chaste tree'.
plato-phaedrus.speaks_note: The made thing here is writing itself, which Socrates says 'cannot answer' when questioned (275d).

confucius-analects.place_label: Qufu, in the state of Lu
confucius-analects.place_note: Compiled and edited by disciples after Confucius's death in 479 BCE, over the Warring States period; Confucius was born in Zou, in modern Qufu, in Lu, and taught there. Where the compilation happened is not recorded.
confucius-analects.opened: Wikipedia 'Analects' ('collected and jointly edited by the disciples after Confucius' death in 479 BCE'); 'Confucius' ('born ... in Zou (陬, in modern Qufu, Shandong)').
confucius-analects.speaks_note: No made being; a record of conversation.

shelley-frankenstein-1818.place_label: Cologny near Geneva, Villa Diodati (begun); London (published)
shelley-frankenstein-1818.place_note: Begun in the summer of 1816 at Villa Diodati by Lake Geneva; much of it written in Bath later that year; published in London on 1 January 1818 by Lackington, Hughes, Harding, Mavor & Jones.
shelley-frankenstein-1818.opened: Wikipedia 'Frankenstein': began 'during summer 1816 at Villa Diodati by Lake Geneva'; 'wrote much of the novel in Bath'; published by 'Lackington, Hughes, Harding, Mavor, & Jones', London.
shelley-frankenstein-1818.speaks_note: The creature learns language and speaks for six chapters.

wilde-dorian-gray.place_note: Wilde's home from 1884 and in the 1891 census was 16 Tite Street, Chelsea; the novel first appeared in Lippincott's Monthly Magazine, Philadelphia, July 1890.
wilde-dorian-gray.opened: Wikipedia 'Oscar Wilde' ('The 1891 census records the Wildes' residence at 16 Tite Street'); 'Lippincott's Monthly Magazine' ('Based in Philadelphia'; 'The Picture of Dorian Gray (July 1890)').
wilde-dorian-gray.speaks_note: The portrait changes but never speaks.

wilde-critic-as-artist.place_note: The Nineteenth Century, a London monthly founded by James Knowles in 1877 and published by Kegan Paul, printed the essay in July and September 1890; Wilde was living at Tite Street.
wilde-critic-as-artist.opened: Wikipedia 'The Nineteenth Century (periodical)' ('a British monthly literary magazine founded in 1877 by James Knowles'); web search summary of the DNB entry for Charles Kegan Paul (publisher of The Nineteenth Century from 1877).
wilde-critic-as-artist.speaks_note: A dialogue about criticism; no made being.

bergson-laughter.place_note: Three articles in the Revue de Paris (Paris), February–March 1899; book 1900.
bergson-laughter.opened: Wikipedia 'Laughter (Bergson)' ('first published in the French review Revue de Paris'); 'Revue de Paris' (a Paris magazine, 1829–1970).
bergson-laughter.speaks_note: 'Something mechanical encrusted upon the living' is the thesis, not a character.

capek-rur.place_note: Čapek worked on R.U.R. at the spa town of Trenčianske Teplice in 1919–20, where his father was the spa doctor (Slovak press accounts); Aventinum published it in Prague in 1920; the world premiere was in Hradec Králové on 2 January 1921.
capek-rur.opened: Wikipedia 'R.U.R.' (first edition 'Aventinum, Prague, 1920'; 'world premiere on 2 January 1921 in Hradec Králové'); web search summary of gregi.net and senior.sk (R.U.R. begun at Trenčianske Teplice).
capek-rur.speaks_note: The robots speak; the word 'robot' enters the language here.

whale-frankenstein-film.place_note: Produced by Universal Pictures, whose lot has stood at Universal City since 1915; released 21 November 1931 and opened in New York at the Mayfair on 4 December. The article does not state where it was shot.
whale-frankenstein-film.opened: Wikipedia 'Frankenstein (1931 film)' ('Produced and distributed by Universal Pictures'); 'Universal City, California' ('officially opened the Second Universal City (Lankershim Boulevard) on March 15, 1915').
whale-frankenstein-film.speaks_note: Karloff's Monster grunts; he first speaks in the 1935 sequel.

eliza.geocode_query: Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge, Massachusetts
eliza.place_note: Developed 1964–67 at MIT by Joseph Weizenbaum; published January 1966.
eliza.opened: Wikipedia 'ELIZA': 'developed from 1964 to 1967 at MIT by Joseph Weizenbaum'.

shrdlu.geocode_query: Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge, Massachusetts
shrdlu.place_note: Developed by Terry Winograd at MIT, 1968–70.
shrdlu.opened: Wikipedia 'SHRDLU': 'developed by Terry Winograd at MIT in 1968–1970'; 'the user carries on a conversation with the computer'.
shrdlu.speaks_note: English conversation about a blocks world.

parry.place_note: Written in 1972 by Kenneth Colby at Stanford; talked to ELIZA over the ARPANET at ICCC 1972.
parry.opened: Wikipedia 'PARRY': 'written in 1972 by psychiatrist Kenneth Colby, then at Stanford University'.
parry.speaks_note: A simulated paranoid patient; the first machine-to-machine conversation.

loebner-prize.place_note: First contest held 8 November 1991 at the Computer Museum, Boston (verified in the timeline (maps/02-ai-and-literature-timeline) against Computer Museum News and Shieber).
loebner-prize.opened: The timeline (maps/02-ai-and-literature-timeline)'s check note ('First contest held 8 November 1991 at the Computer Museum, Boston').
loebner-prize.speaks_note: A Turing-test contest for chat programs.

siri.place_label: Cupertino, Apple (announced); originated at SRI, Menlo Park
siri.place_note: Announced by Apple (Cupertino) with the iPhone 4S on 4 October 2011; the technology was spun out of SRI International's Artificial Intelligence Center in Menlo Park in 2007 and acquired by Apple in 2010.
siri.opened: Wikipedia 'Siri' ('a spin-out from the Stanford Research Institute's Artificial Intelligence Center'); 'SRI International' ('headquarters are located in Menlo Park'); 'Apple Inc.' (headquarters 'Apple Park, Cupertino').

gpt-2.place_note: OpenAI has been based in San Francisco since at least September 2016 (Pioneer Building, Mission District; now Third Street). The organisation's city, not a documented lab room.
gpt-2.opened: Wikipedia 'OpenAI' (headquarters 'San Francisco, California'; 'moved to the Pioneer Building in San Francisco's Mission District in September 2016').
gpt-2.speaks_note: Generates text; the staged release was about what it could say.

chatgpt.speaks_note: The chat interface that made the assistant a mass medium.

claude-code.place_note: Anthropic's headquarters city. Included because it is the conversational agent this seminar uses.
claude-code.speaks_note: A coding agent you talk to in a terminal.

added.title: Kempelen's speaking machine, described in print
added.description: A bellows, a reed, and a leather mouth worked by hand to produce words and short sentences. Kempelen began it in 1769 and described it in a 456-page book with 27 plates, published in Vienna in 1791: the first machine built to speak, as opposed to play or write.
added.place_label: Vienna (J. B. Degen, publisher of the 1791 book)
added.place_note: The book describing the machine was published in Vienna by J. B. Degen in 1791 (MPI and HathiTrust catalogue records). Kempelen was a Vienna court official who divided his life between Vienna and Pressburg; where the machine itself was assembled is not stated.
added.opened: Wikipedia 'Wolfgang von Kempelen's speaking machine' ('began development in 1769'; the 456-page book of 1791); web search summary of the MPI and HathiTrust records (Vienna: Degen, 1791).
added.speaks_note: Built to pronounce words; the operator plays it like an instrument.

added.title: Faber's Euphonia
added.description: A talking machine with a mask-like face, keyboard, bellows, and artificial tongue that could pronounce sentences in a monotone and, with effort, sing. Faber, an Austrian inventor, exhibited it in Philadelphia in 1845 and at the Egyptian Hall in London in 1846.
added.place_note: Exhibited in 1845 in Philadelphia and in 1846 at London's Egyptian Hall; where it was built is not stated.
added.opened: Wikipedia 'Euphonia (device)': 'exhibited in 1845 in Philadelphia and in 1846 in London's Egyptian Hall'.
added.speaks_note: Speech in a sepulchral monotone, by all accounts.

added.title: The Voder (Bell Labs)
added.description: The first electronic speech synthesizer, which broke speech into acoustic components that a trained operator recombined with keys and a pedal. Invented by Homer Dudley in 1937–38 and performed at the 1939 New York World's Fair and in San Francisco.
added.place_label: New York World's Fair, Flushing Meadows (exhibited); built at Bell Labs, 463 West Street, New York
added.geocode_query: Flushing Meadows–Corona Park, Queens, New York
added.place_note: Demonstrated at the 1939 New York World's Fair (and in San Francisco); Bell Labs then worked from 463 West Street in Manhattan, before the move to Murray Hill.
added.opened: Wikipedia 'Voder' ('invented by Homer Dudley in 1937–1938'; 'featured at the 1939 New York World's Fair and in San Francisco'); 'Bell Labs' (463 West Street; headquarters formally moved to Murray Hill only in 1967).
added.speaks_note: Electronic speech, played by an operator.

added.title: Xiaoice
added.description: A social chatbot built on an 'emotional computing framework', launched in China in 2014 and designed for long, companionable conversation rather than tasks; it later wrote poetry and hosted television.
added.place_note: Developed by Microsoft's Software Technology Center Asia, established December 2013 with operations across Beijing, Suzhou, and Tokyo; Beijing is the base. The article does not pin the team to one city.
added.opened: Wikipedia 'Xiaoice': 'developed by Microsoft (Asia) Software Technology Center (STCA) in 2014'; STCA 'operations distributed across Beijing, Suzhou, and Tokyo'.
added.speaks_note: Text and voice conversation with hundreds of millions of users.

added.title: Amazon Alexa, announced with the Echo
added.description: A voice assistant in a cylinder on the kitchen counter, built from the acquired Evi question-answering system and the Ivona speech synthesizer. Announced on 6 November 2014 with the Echo.
added.place_note: Developed at Amazon Lab126, 1100 Enterprise Way, Sunnyvale; Amazon itself is in Seattle.
added.opened: Wikipedia 'Amazon Alexa' ('On November 6, 2014, Amazon announced Alexa alongside the Echo'; developed by Lab126); 'Amazon Lab126' ('1100 Enterprise Way, Sunnyvale, California 94089').
